questions.q: A SageMaker training job cannot read your S3 dataset, although you can open the bucket yourself. What is the most likely cause?
options: S3 blocks all training jobs by design
The execution role the job runs as lacks permission for that bucket
Your IAM user has too many permissions
Parquet files cannot be read by SageMaker
questions.explain: Jobs run as the execution role, not as you. The role needs its own permissions on the bucket.

questions.q: Which service principal appears in the trust policy of a SageMaker execution role?
questions.explain: The documented trust policy names sagemaker.amazonaws.com with the sts:AssumeRole action, so the SageMaker service can assume the role.

questions.q: According to the AWS docs, AmazonSageMakerFullAccess grants certain S3 actions on buckets whose names contain which words?
questions.explain: The managed policy's S3 object access is limited by bucket name. For other buckets you attach an additional policy that names them.

questions.q: What is the best way to grant a training role access to project data?
options: Give it S3 access to every bucket with a wildcard
Scope actions to the project prefixes, with raw data read-only
questions.explain: Least privilege means only the actions and resources the job needs: read raw, read and write processed and models, and list with a prefix condition.

questions.q: What does iam:PassRole with an iam:PassedToService condition of sagemaker.amazonaws.com allow?
options: Passing the named role to SageMaker only
questions.explain: PassRole lets you hand a role to a service when you start a job. The condition limits it to SageMaker, and naming one role in Resource narrows it further.
